clue.text: In country dance, become friendlier with a writer’s partner

blocks.note: relations thaw when two people warm to each other
the article taken as it stands, tacked on after the thaw
the hay is an old English country dance with weaving figures

explanation.surface: Two people at a village barn dance slowly warming to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Shakespeare, and his partner is his wife Anne. The hay, an old round dance, is rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway married William Shakespeare in 1582, so she is the playwright's wife, his spouse.

clue.text: Who may put out pile of fodder?

indicators.note: someone put out is disturbed, so the letters are disturbed from their order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A farmyard question: whose job is it to set out the animals' feed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who may put out' reads as the start of a question about a farmhand, but 'put out' means disturbed, so the first two words are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymow is a stack of hay, or the barn loft where it is stored, kept as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Served up repeatedly one kind of meat or fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is served up is sent upward, read from the bottom

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
ham is cured pork, one sort of meat
the same pair of pieces taken a second time

explanation.surface: A waiter bringing out the same dish again and again, meat or fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' turns the pieces upward, and 'repeatedly' asks for the result twice. 'Meat or fish' looks like a menu choice, but 'or' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahi-mahi is a warm-water game species, also sold as dorado or dolphinfish, common on restaurant menus.

clue.text: Personal decoration in military display

blocks.note: ink worked into the skin as body art
an evening show of marching bands and drill, like the Edinburgh one

explanation.surface: A soldier showing off body art at a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses come from different words: skin art from Polynesian 'tatau', the military show from a Dutch drum call closing the taps of the taverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink designs on skin adorn the wearer; a military tattoo is an outdoor show of massed bands and drill.

clue.text: Landing-place for rescue craft with full complement of mates

definitions.text: Landing-place for rescue craft with full complement of mates

blocks.note: on the surface, a helipad or a slipway for a lifeboat
the setter means Noah's ark, carrying every animal two by two, coming to rest on a mountain

explanation.surface: A harbour where a lifeboat puts in with its whole crew aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mates' sounds like shipmates, but it means breeding pairs: the ark took every creature in twos. Genesis says it came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis places the ark's grounding after the Flood on this Turkish peak, making it the vessel's berth.

clue.text: Loss of control in vehicle covered by motoring organization

blocks.note: the Automobile Association, Britain's breakdown-recovery club
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car skidding out of control, with the breakdown service insuring it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a driver losing control of a car, but the loss is of the body: the clue's first words are the definition, a medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is the medical term for impaired coordination of bodily movements, often from nerve damage.

clue.text: Empty small container into large container

indicators.note: emptying one thing into another puts it inside

blocks.note: a vat is a big tank for brewing or dyeing
a tin can is a small receptacle

explanation.surface: Tipping the contents of a tin into a big tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like a verb telling you to pour, but it is the adjective, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant describes a room or seat with nobody or nothing in it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A motto represented in bright shade of red

indicators.note: re-presented: the same letters presented again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the article plus the saying, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A family motto painted in heraldic red on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' reads as depicted, but here it means presented again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato red is a named colour, the vivid scarlet of the ripe fruit's skin.

clue.text: Seeking all-round balance, I rig a neat arrangement around a line

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed on either side, surrounding the short pair

blocks.note: four words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange
the article taken as it stands
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone fixing a tidy set-up to keep things level all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig' suggests cheating, which is the opposite of the fair-mindedness defined. 'A line' is two pieces, the article and the abbreviation, and they sit in the middle of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian wants equal rights and shares for everyone, a society balanced across all its members.

clue.text: Have deep understanding of female leading most of party in house

indicators.note: the woman goes in front, at the head of what follows

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
an at-home is a party given in one's own house; drop its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman hosting most of a house party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party in house' is one piece, an at-home, a rather old-fashioned word for a reception held at home. 'Deep' in the definition nods to the fathom as a unit of sea depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to grasp it thoroughly, originally by sounding the water's depth.

clue.text: I’m eating frantically? Deliberately slow down

indicators.note: done in a frenzy, the letters are thrown about into a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone bolting food who is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets a frantic eater against a call to slow down; the question mark signals the pun. The definition is the second sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain time is to stall or delay on purpose, buying extra room to act.

clue.text: Watch that is found in car

blocks.note: a Volkswagen, known by its initials
i.e., Latin id est, meaning 'that is'

explanation.surface: A wristwatch left behind in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' reads as a noun, a timepiece, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to look at it, as one looks on as a spectator.

clue.text: Steps taken by royalty and a bishop in quitting protests

indicators.note: the royal pair of pieces goes inside the protest word

blocks.note: strikes where workers leave the building together
the article taken as it stands
chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: The monarch and a bishop resigning in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' is literal: a royal walkabout is the monarch strolling among the crowd, shaking hands. 'Quitting protests' is one piece, the walkouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkabouts are informal strolls among crowds by a monarch or dignitary, meeting the public face to face.

clue.text: Return writing including my revised article showing result of reflection

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the combined piece reads backwards
a revised piece of text has been reworked, its letters reordered

blocks.note: short for manuscript
the word taken as it stands
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending back a manuscript with my rewritten piece tucked inside, a thoughtful result.
explanation.walkthrough: MS holds MY to make MMYS, which runs backwards as SYMM; ARTICLE reshuffled gives the rest. 'Reflection' looks like deep thought, but it is a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror image repeats a shape exactly on the other side of an axis, so each half matches.

clue.text: Four thousand and three articles I recollected? Good heavens!

indicators.note: re-collected: gathered together again in a different order

blocks.note: M is the Roman thousand, taken four times
the indefinite article, three times
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: Someone astonished at remembering a huge number of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split it: re-collected, gathered again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamma mia is an Italian exclamation of surprise or dismay, literally 'my mother', used like 'my goodness'.

clue.text: Robotic workforce which singularly includes 7

blocks.note: a team of machines doing the work
the singular form of the plural holds the answer to 7 down, a red fruit, spelt inside it

explanation.surface: A factory of robots with a curious feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular is AUTOMATON, and AU-TOMATO-N contains the answer to 7, TOMATO. 'Singularly' reads as 'remarkably' but means 'in the singular'.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are self-operating machines, robots, and a collection of them makes up a mechanical labour force.

clue.text: Fail to include covering time after time for bird

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, the one that comes first
to omit is to leave out
the same abbreviation, the one being covered

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly failing to tuck a bird in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' looks like one phrase meaning repeatedly; it splits, the first time being covered and the second coming before. A tomtit is a small titmouse, often the blue tit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomtit is a familiar British name for small tits, especially the blue tit, a garden songbird.

clue.text: A measure of power – nothing upset capital

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so in a down clue it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the SI unit of power
zero, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A political power gauge showing the capital's influence falling to zero.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the pieces upside down, so they read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the seat of Canada's federal government, the country's chief city of administration.

clue.text: Exercise for troops, English, in month after Waterloo

blocks.note: Napoleon's crushing defeat, so any rout
standard abbreviation
the third month of the year

explanation.surface: British soldiers drilling in the month after the famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterloo' is a lower-case word here: to meet one's Waterloo is to suffer a decisive defeat, a rout. It is a date clue in disguise, and the battle was in June, not February.
explanation.definitionFit: A route march is a long training walk soldiers make in formation to build stamina.

clue.text: Kind of radio to evaluate, roughly speaking

indicators.note: 'speaking' points to how the phrase is said, and 'roughly' admits the match is only by ear

blocks.note: to weigh something up is to evaluate it

explanation.surface: Judging the quality of a radio in rough terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly speaking' passes for 'approximately', but it points to speech: say the phrase for evaluating and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-way radio both transmits and receives, like a walkie-talkie, unlike a broadcast receiver.

clue.text: Fruit a couple of Romans found in this state

blocks.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
taken as it stands
two Roman ones, the numeral for two

explanation.surface: Tourists from Rome finding exotic fruit in the island state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' suggests the pineapples of the islands, but it is the humble hawthorn berry. 'Romans' are Roman numerals, one each.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii is the fiftieth American state, the Pacific island group admitted in 1959.

clue.text: Dance outfit with identical halves, though not 13

definitions.text: Dance outfit with identical halves, though not 13

blocks.note: the stiff skirt a ballerina wears
the word is two equal halves, yet it is not a mirror image, so not the answer to 13 across

explanation.surface: A costume whose two sides match but which is somehow lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: The description is of the word, not the garment: TU plus TU, repeated rather than reversed, so it does not read the same backwards and is not SYMMETRICAL, the answer to 13.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt of net layers that ballet dancers wear on stage.

clue.text: Body tissues doctor turned over put in layers

blocks.note: medical officer, a military doctor
strata are layers, as of rock

explanation.surface: A doctor who turns a patient over to examine layers of tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is medical from start to finish, which hides the fact that 'layers' is plain wordplay, a geology word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromata are the supporting connective frameworks of organs, the plural of stroma in anatomy.

clue.text: Animal in our original environment, area with reduced temperature

blocks.note: the first place any of us lived
standard abbreviation
temperature cut down to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: An animal in its native habitat, cooling as the climate changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our original environment' reads like a habitat, but it is where each of us began, before birth. 'Reduced temperature' is not cold weather but a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial, a stocky creature of the bush.

clue.text: Unhappy indication of nervousness about fundraiser

blocks.note: a nervous tic is an involuntary twitch
a rag is a British student charity event, with stunts and collections

explanation.surface: Someone twitching anxiously over a charity appeal that went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is British student slang: rag week is when students raise money for charity with stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events end in grief or disaster, a stronger sense than merely sad.

clue.text: Other instruments replacing sitars

indicators.note: re-placing: putting the letters in new places

blocks.note: the Indian stringed instruments, letter for letter

explanation.surface: An orchestra swapping out its Indian stringed instruments for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'replacing' as re-placing: putting the letters in new places. The definition is 'Other instruments', fair because sitars are instruments too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra, plural of sistrum, are ancient Egyptian metal rattles shaken in temple rites.
